description: Fictional support tickets for a fictional B2B analytics SaaS product, for prototype development and evaluation only.

generation_method.text: Written by four parallel language-model agents (Claude), three categories each, from one shared specification (category boundaries, content rules, diversity and relationship targets, exclusions), in batches with self-checks. The text is not reproducible.
generation_method.ordering: Python random.Random(20261117).shuffle over the 960 generated records in category order (auth, sync, render, billing, export, perm, perf, api, alerts, data_quality, connectivity, workspace_admin), then ids assigned sequentially from T-2001. Reproducible given the same batch files.
generation_method.originals: The 40 records of starter_kit/data/tickets.json are first, unchanged and in their original order.
generation_method.exclusions: No Snowflake or data-warehouse destination incidents, so the incoming Snowflake example keeps no historical answer.

category_boundaries.alerts: Metric threshold rules, alert triggering, suppression, missed and duplicate alerts. Password-reset emails stay auth; scheduled report delivery stays export.
category_boundaries.data_quality: Incorrect values, calculations, units, mappings or aggregations after successful ingestion. Failed or missing ingestion stays sync.
category_boundaries.connectivity: DNS, proxies, firewalls, TLS configuration and network reachability. Credential problems stay auth or the relevant integration category.
category_boundaries.workspace_admin: Workspace identity, branding, locale, preferences and organizational settings. Access permissions stay perm; charges and subscriptions stay billing.

auth.name: Password reset links invalidated or rejected
auth.summary: Single-use reset tokens are consumed or broken before the user redeems them (mail link scanners, superseded requests, redirects or line-wrapping that strip the token); users see 'already used', 'expired' or 'invalid token'.
auth.boundary_note: Credential recovery is part of signing in, so auth; it is not export or alerts even though an email carries the link.

auth.name: Password reset email not delivered or suppressed
auth.summary: Reset emails that are deferred, misrouted, suppressed by design for SSO-enforced accounts, rate-limited or never generated because of a template fault.
auth.boundary_note: Password-reset emails stay auth by policy; scheduled report emails are export and metric notifications are alerts.

auth.name: SAML assertion, attribute and endpoint mapping
auth.summary: Mismatched entity IDs, ACS URLs, NameID formats, clock skew or assertion parsing faults cause SSO errors or unmatched users.
auth.boundary_note: The failure happens at sign-in before any role is evaluated (not perm) and no network path is blocked (not connectivity).

auth.name: SSO signing certificate rotation and mix-ups
auth.summary: Identity provider or service provider signing certificates are rotated, renewed or uploaded wrongly, so assertion or request signatures fail and every SSO user is affected at once.
auth.boundary_note: These certificates sign SSO messages; they are sign-in credentials, not TLS/network certificates, so auth rather than connectivity.

auth.name: OIDC client configuration
auth.summary: Expired client secrets, unregistered redirect URIs, missing scopes or oversized tokens break OpenID Connect sign-in.
auth.boundary_note: This is people signing in through OIDC, not an integration calling the public API, so auth rather than api.

auth.name: Authenticator (TOTP) code verification
auth.summary: One-time codes are rejected because of device clock drift, stale enrollment secrets after device migration, input formatting or expired enrollment QR codes.
auth.boundary_note: Second-factor verification during login is auth.

auth.name: Two-factor enforcement and recovery
auth.summary: Problems rolling out mandatory 2FA, recovery codes, trusted-device cookies and owner resets of a lost second factor.
auth.boundary_note: Concerns sign-in requirements and recovery rather than what a role may access (perm).

auth.name: Account lockouts from stale or automated credentials
auth.summary: Lockout policy tripped by scripts, cached add-in passwords or kiosk autofill, lockouts extended by repeated attempts, or lockouts that actually originate at the identity provider.
auth.boundary_note: Lockout is a sign-in control; it is not offboarding or role management (perm).

auth.name: Session lifetime and multi-workspace sessions
auth.summary: Sessions ending earlier than users expect due to absolute versus idle limits, workspace switching, client clock errors, persistent-session policy or unattended screens.
auth.boundary_note: Session validity is auth; slow pages are perf and wrongly drawn dashboards are render.

auth.name: Browser cookie handling and login loops
auth.summary: Login loops or silent failures from third-party cookie blocking in embedded views, cookie name collisions on custom domains, blocked browser storage or managed cookie policies.
auth.boundary_note: The browser drops or never stores the session; the dashboard itself renders fine once signed in (not render) and no proxy or firewall is involved (not connectivity).

auth.name: Invitation acceptance and account activation
auth.summary: Invitation and activation links that expire, are consumed early, attach to the wrong identity or fail because of malformed addresses.
auth.boundary_note: Creating a user's sign-in identity is auth; what they can see once activated is perm.

auth.name: Sign-in identity matching
auth.summary: Users reach a new, empty or no account because their email, alias, letter case or domain differs from the stored login identity.
auth.boundary_note: Users may see empty workspaces, but the cause is which identity they signed in as, not role assignment, so auth rather than perm.

auth.name: Personal access tokens for user tools
auth.summary: Personal tokens used by the spreadsheet add-in or command-line tool are rejected after password changes, expiry, workspace scoping or blocked sign-in pop-ups.
auth.boundary_note: These tokens authenticate an individual user, so auth; keys used by system integrations against the public API are api.

auth.name: Mobile app sign-in
auth.summary: Biometric unlock, SSO hand-back to the app, cached workspace lookups, token persistence and sign-out on shared devices in the mobile app.
auth.boundary_note: Sign-in and session behaviour in the mobile app are auth; mobile chart layout would be render.

auth.name: Password policy and forced password changes
auth.summary: Complexity rules, breach screening, expiry loops, Unicode normalization and policy changes that reject passwords or trap users in change prompts.
auth.boundary_note: Credential rules are auth, distinct from general workspace defaults (workspace_admin).

sync.name: Connector authorization expired or revoked
sync.summary: OAuth grants or stored credentials used by an inbound connector are revoked, expire, rotate or lose scope (authorizing user deactivated, password rotation, short token lifetimes), so syncs fail or quietly return nothing.
sync.boundary_note: The credential is the connector's access to the source system, not a person signing in to our app (auth) or a client calling our public API (api).

sync.name: Stuck or hung sync jobs
sync.summary: Runs that never finish: orphaned job locks, crashed workers with no heartbeat, endless loops on bad source data, source requests without timeouts, or two jobs deadlocking.
sync.boundary_note: The stuck work is ingestion from a source; general application slowness under load would be perf.

sync.name: Duplicate records from ingestion
sync.summary: Records inserted twice because source IDs change on merge or re-import, ingestion paths use different keys, overlapping windows lack a unique key, or file uploads append instead of replace.
sync.boundary_note: The duplicates are created by ingestion itself, so sync rather than data_quality, which covers wrong calculations on correctly ingested data.

sync.name: Incremental cursor gaps
sync.summary: Incremental syncs skip records because the source does not update modification timestamps, records arrive late or backdated, or the cursor mishandles local time.
sync.boundary_note: The records are never ingested, which stays sync even when time zones are involved; mis-bucketing of ingested data would be data_quality.

sync.name: Pagination and truncated pulls
sync.summary: Source offset caps, expiring page tokens, truncated nested records, unstable sort orders and page-count safeguards make a sync stop early while reporting success.
sync.boundary_note: Data is missing because the pull from the source was incomplete; this is ingestion, not a fault in our own public API (api).

sync.name: Source schema changes
sync.summary: Renamed, deleted or retyped source fields, retired source API versions and new picklist values break field mappings, fail runs or blank values.
sync.boundary_note: The value never arrives because the mapping broke during ingestion, so sync rather than data_quality.

sync.name: File-based ingestion (CSV uploads and SFTP drops)
sync.summary: Encoding, delimiter and decimal conventions, file-name patterns and partially written files cause rejected, garbled or incomplete imports of customer-supplied files.
sync.boundary_note: These are inbound files being ingested; CSV or Excel files produced by our app are export.

sync.name: Source API quotas and throttling
sync.summary: Customer-side API allowances or source rate limits are exhausted by other tools, peak traffic or backfills, so runs stop, lag or are skipped.
sync.boundary_note: The limits are imposed by the source on our connector, not our public API rate limits (api); the delay is in ingestion rather than app performance (perf).

sync.name: Deletions, cancellations and edits not propagated
sync.summary: Hard deletes, cancellations, standalone refunds, archived items and post-fulfilment adjustments are never fetched, leaving stale records in dashboards.
sync.boundary_note: Totals look wrong because state changes were never ingested, so sync rather than data_quality.

sync.name: Sync scheduling and auto-pause
sync.summary: Schedules auto-paused after failures with notices sent to inactive recipients, schedules in the wrong time zone, frequency lost after a plan change, and runs skipped at daylight-saving transitions.
sync.boundary_note: This is about when ingestion runs: not alert rules (alerts), not workspace time-zone preferences (workspace_admin), and no charge is wrong (billing).

sync.name: Connector access scope in the source system
sync.summary: Integration users or app installs lack read access to regions, objects, fields or scopes in the source, so part of the data arrives and part does not.
sync.boundary_note: The permissions live in the customer's source system and govern what the connector can read; roles inside our app are perm.

sync.name: Source account, store and instance selection
sync.summary: The connector points at the wrong instance (sandbox or decommissioned) or omits new stores, storefronts or advertising accounts.
sync.boundary_note: Data never ingested from the right source account is sync, not a reporting or permission issue.

sync.name: Initial historical backfill
sync.summary: First loads with a short default history, run-duration caps, non-resumable retries, mismatched object coverage, or backfills that block daily syncs.
sync.boundary_note: Concerns the initial ingestion of history, so sync; app-wide slowness on large datasets is perf.

sync.name: Inbound event (webhook) ingestion
sync.summary: Real-time events from source platforms are rejected after signing-secret rotation, lost when subscriptions disappear or intake overflows, or never registered for added stores; data then arrives only with the scheduled catch-up sync.
sync.boundary_note: These are inbound events used to ingest source data, so sync; our outbound webhooks and public API belong to api.

render.name: Empty or blank charts
render.summary: Charts draw nothing, not even axes, for all-null series, broken field references, negative values in stacked charts or formatter failures, instead of showing a clear empty state.
render.boundary_note: The data is present or legitimately empty; the failure is in drawing it. Missing ingestion would be sync and wrong values would be data_quality.

render.name: Stale visuals and caching
render.summary: Users see out-of-date charts, layouts, previews or app versions because of service worker bundles, query result caches, thumbnail generation or browser caching of dashboard definitions.
render.boundary_note: The underlying data was ingested and is correct; only what is displayed is stale, so render rather than sync.

render.name: Filters not applying to widgets
render.summary: Dashboard, cross-filter, store and shared-link filters do not reach widgets because of pinned ranges, field mappings, name matching or filter state that is not carried along.
render.boundary_note: Users have access and queries are fast; the view simply does not reflect the filter, so render rather than perm or perf.

render.name: Layout, overlap and responsive grid
render.summary: Widgets overlap, overflow, refuse to resize or waste space at different display scaling, screen widths and devices.
render.boundary_note: On-screen arrangement only; workspace defaults and branding are workspace_admin.

render.name: On-screen number and label formatting
render.summary: Axis abbreviations, tooltip formats, negative-number style, truncated labels and decimal precision displayed wrongly while the values themselves are right.
render.boundary_note: Values are correct and settings are saved; the display layer formats them wrongly, so render rather than data_quality or workspace_admin.

render.name: Series colours and legends
render.summary: Colours assigned by position instead of category value, brand palettes not applied to charts, and legends swamping charts with many series.
render.boundary_note: A visual-encoding problem; saving the brand colours themselves is workspace_admin.

render.name: Browser- and device-specific rendering
render.summary: Canvas size limits in Safari and on iPads, content-blocking extensions and pixel-ratio changes across monitors make charts blank or blurry on particular setups.
render.boundary_note: No proxy or firewall is involved (connectivity) and nothing is slow (perf); drawing fails on specific clients.

render.name: Embedded dashboard display
render.summary: Embedded dashboards cut off, scaled down, themed or filtered wrongly inside customer portals, or flickering in resize loops.
render.boundary_note: The embed is signed in; the issues are sizing, theme and display parameters. Login loops inside embeds are auth.

render.name: Time-axis display
render.summary: Axis labels shifted by the viewer's time zone, ambiguous repeated daylight-saving hours, skipped month ticks and missing dates drawn as zero.
render.boundary_note: The data is bucketed correctly; only the labels or the drawing are wrong, so render rather than data_quality.

render.name: Map and geo visuals
render.summary: Store maps and region maps missing pins or regions, missing background tiles, overlapping pins and auto-zoom to empty coordinates.
render.boundary_note: Map lookup and drawing problems, not wrong sales values (data_quality) or blocked networks (connectivity).

render.name: Table and pivot widgets
render.summary: Column and row misalignment in virtualized tables under browser zoom, wrong totals-row labels, missing conditional formatting and sticky headers lost in full screen.
render.boundary_note: On-screen table display; downloading table contents is export.

render.name: Widget loading failures and error states
render.summary: Widgets stuck loading or whole pages failing because of removed code chunks after releases, uncontained widget errors, unusual characters or blocked web workers.
render.boundary_note: The failure is in the front end rather than a slow query (perf) or missing data (sync).

render.name: TV and kiosk display mode
render.summary: Shop-floor screens that freeze, skip dashboards in rotation, scale badly on 4K or wide screens, or go dark.
render.boundary_note: Display-mode behaviour; a session expiring on an unattended screen is auth.

render.name: Dark mode, theme and contrast
render.summary: Hard-coded colours make labels, cells, chips or series invisible in dark theme, on brand palettes or in high-contrast mode.
render.boundary_note: Visual contrast on screen; configuring the theme or branding itself is workspace_admin.

render.name: Tooltips, drill-down and chart interactions
render.summary: Tooltips showing the wrong item or drifting from the pointer, drill-downs opening the wrong category, missing touch interaction and zoom lost on refresh.
render.boundary_note: Interaction with drawn charts; the data and permissions behind them are correct.

billing.name: Seat counting and reconciliation
billing.summary: The billed seat quantity differs from the customer's own count because of how seats are counted: pending invitations, viewer accounts on plans where viewers are billable, automation users, or workspaces not linked to the billing account. Symptoms are invoices or quotes with more or fewer seats than active users.
billing.boundary_note: The dispute is about the quantity charged, not about what users can access, so it is billing rather than perm.

billing.name: Mid-cycle proration
billing.summary: Prorated amounts for upgrades, seat additions or add-ons are computed from the wrong start date, the wrong price tier or across a billing-timezone boundary, or an expected credit for a reduction does not appear.
billing.boundary_note: Concerns how charges are calculated and when they are invoiced; no data, display or access defect is involved.

billing.name: Plan changes, pauses and cancellations
billing.summary: Upgrades, downgrades, pauses or cancellations do not take effect, take effect at the wrong time, apply to the wrong workspace, or are blocked by a pending condition. Symptoms include billing on the old plan, features lost early or an unwanted renewal.
billing.boundary_note: Feature changes here are driven by subscription state rather than roles or settings, so billing rather than perm or workspace_admin.

billing.name: Discounts, coupons and negotiated pricing
billing.summary: Discounts missing, expired early, applied to the wrong lines or applied without entitlement, often because the discount was stored on one subscription term instead of the account.
billing.boundary_note: Pricing adjustments on invoices and at checkout are billing by definition.

billing.name: Payment method updates and card authorization
billing.summary: Adding or replacing a payment method fails or silently does not stick because of strong customer authentication challenges, issuer restrictions or unsupported payment types.
billing.boundary_note: Concerns the payment method on the subscription; browser or issuer behaviour is only the trigger, so it is not connectivity or auth.

billing.name: Failed payments, dunning and account holds
billing.summary: Accounts placed on hold, reminders missed, or holds not lifted because of failed renewals, outdated billing contacts, unmatched bank transfers or wrong payment terms.
billing.boundary_note: Users may lose edit capability, but the cause is the payment state, so billing rather than perm.

billing.name: Charges that look duplicated
billing.summary: Two charges that appear to be duplicates but come from card verification authorizations, separate subscriptions, overlapping billing periods after a cycle switch, duplicate orders or a double-submitted payment page.
billing.boundary_note: Charge disputes are billing; each case has a cause distinct from a single subscription being charged twice by an automatic payment retry.

billing.name: Sales tax and VAT
billing.summary: Tax applied when it should not be, or missing when it should be, because of VAT ID validation, the address used to determine tax jurisdiction, exemption certificates not attached, or the billing entity on the account.
billing.boundary_note: Tax on our invoices is a billing matter; it does not involve tax values inside the customer's analytics data.

billing.name: Invoice documents and invoice delivery
billing.summary: Invoices missing required references, carrying outdated legal details, not reaching the right contacts, not downloadable, or not present because the purchase was made through a marketplace.
billing.boundary_note: Invoice notifications and documents are billing, not scheduled report delivery (export) or workspace identity (workspace_admin).

billing.name: Billing currency and monetary formatting
billing.summary: Invoices or credit notes in the wrong currency, differences between checkout estimates and card charges, and rounding or minor-unit formatting errors on invoice documents.
billing.boundary_note: Currency on prices and invoices is billing; currency of values in analytics data is data_quality.

billing.name: Usage meters and add-on charges
billing.summary: Overage or add-on charges caused by usage meters counting retained, soft-deleted or failed items, or by add-ons triggered automatically or left enabled on another workspace.
billing.boundary_note: Meters may reference connectors or API traffic, but the dispute is the charge, so billing rather than sync or api.

billing.name: Trials, renewals and price protection
billing.summary: Trial conversion surprises or failures, extensions not applied, renewal notices for cancelled workspaces, and renewals or quotes reverting to list price when a contracted price was stored for one term only.
billing.boundary_note: Subscription lifecycle events and renewal pricing are billing.

billing.name: Refunds, credit notes and account balances
billing.summary: Credits not applied or applied to the wrong invoice or workspace, refunds delayed or bouncing, prepaid credits expiring early, and unexpected refunds from bulk corrections.
billing.boundary_note: Money returned to the customer or held on the account is billing.

export.name: Row limits and truncated exports
export.summary: Exports silently capped by file-format or plan limits, per-widget export settings or export-job query time limits, so files arrive with fewer rows than the on-screen data.
export.boundary_note: The problem is an incomplete export file; general slowness under load without a truncated file would be perf.

export.name: Export job processing failures
export.summary: Background export jobs stuck in Preparing, failing on unsupported field types or broken widget content, ignoring cancellation, missing completion notifications or failing without a visible reason.
export.boundary_note: The fault is in the export pipeline itself, not general platform load (perf) or how dashboards display (render).

export.name: Scheduled report timing
export.summary: Scheduled reports sent at the wrong time or day, skipped, duplicated or paused because of fixed UTC offsets across daylight saving changes, month-end rules, copied schedules or deactivated schedule owners.
export.boundary_note: Scheduled report delivery is export by definition; threshold-based metric notifications would be alerts.

export.name: Report email delivery
export.summary: Report emails that do not reach recipients or arrive unusable: single-use links consumed by mail security scanners, recipient domain restrictions, oversized attachments and spam filtering after a sender change.
export.boundary_note: These are report delivery emails, which stay in export; password-reset emails are auth and invoice emails are billing.

export.name: CSV encoding, delimiters and escaping
export.summary: CSV files that open incorrectly in spreadsheet tools or importers because of a missing byte-order mark, a character sanitiser, the delimiter choice or embedded line breaks.
export.boundary_note: The data is correct in the platform; only the export file's encoding or structure is wrong, so export rather than data_quality.

export.name: Export contents differ from the on-screen view
export.summary: Exports that ignore session filters, include hidden columns, use a different sort or omit totals, so the file does not match what the user saw.
export.boundary_note: The dashboard shows the right data; the mismatch is introduced by the export, so export rather than render or data_quality.

export.name: Dates, times and number formats in exported files
export.summary: Timestamps written without offsets, end-exclusive date ranges, locale number formats ignored, currency codes missing, leading zeros stripped or percentages written as fractions in exported files.
export.boundary_note: Values are correct after ingestion; only their representation in the file differs, so export rather than data_quality or workspace_admin.

export.name: PDF export layout and rendering
export.summary: PDF exports with missing or still-loading charts, cut-off wide tables, missing glyphs or display-theme colours unsuitable for print.
export.boundary_note: Dashboards display correctly on screen; only the generated PDF is wrong, so export rather than render.

export.name: Excel workbook specifics
export.summary: XLSX files with dates or numbers stored as text, invalid sheet names, repair prompts, merged header rows or lost cell styling.
export.boundary_note: The problems are specific to the generated workbook, not to the underlying data or the on-screen display.

export.name: Export restrictions, masking and export policies
export.summary: Export menus missing or unexpectedly available, personal data masked or blanked in files, watermarks missing and workspace-wide export freezes, all driven by export policy settings.
export.boundary_note: Export permissions as a feature setting stay in export; general role and sharing problems would be perm.

export.name: Download links and export file access
export.summary: Report and Export Center download links that expire early, are single-use, require sign-in, resolve to the wrong workspace or file, or point to files no longer retained.
export.boundary_note: Concerns access to generated export files, not user login (auth) or role-based access to dashboards (perm).

export.name: Scheduled file drops to SFTP and shared storage
export.summary: Recurring file deliveries to customer-managed SFTP folders or storage buckets that overwrite earlier files, are read half-written, carry the wrong date token, change format or change column layout.
export.boundary_note: These are file-based scheduled exports with delivery-configuration causes, not inbound data sync or network reachability.

export.name: Widget-specific export behaviour
export.summary: Exports from pivot tables, maps, charts, KPI tiles and drill-down tables that produce flattened, empty, image-only, differently rounded or partial output.
export.boundary_note: The widget displays correctly; the issue is what its export produces.

perm.name: Default roles and onboarding access
perm.summary: New or invited users end up with the wrong level of access because team join rules, domain auto-join defaults, import column mapping, the inviting workspace, default-role contents or 'All members' shares override the intended role.
perm.boundary_note: Concerns what new users can access once signed in, not their ability to sign in (auth) or seat charges (billing).

perm.name: Offboarding, transfers and deprovisioning
perm.summary: Access that survives deactivation, deprovisioning or internal moves (public links from departed users, leftover folder grants, SCIM deactivation ignored, direct grants after a region change) or content hidden when its owner is removed.
perm.boundary_note: Revoking or moving access rights is perm; invalidating sign-in sessions alone would be auth.

perm.name: Identity provider group and role mapping
perm.summary: Group-to-role mappings that stop matching or resolve to the wrong role because of case-sensitive names, nested groups, precedence rules or enforcement on every sign-in.
perm.boundary_note: Users sign in successfully; the defect is the role assigned from directory groups, so perm rather than auth.

perm.name: Dashboard sharing
perm.summary: Shares that do not give working access: datasets not shared with the dashboard, cross-team sharing policy, locked filters on a share, public links disabled by policy, shares expanded to individuals, or shares sent to mailing-list addresses.
perm.boundary_note: Sharing is an access-right feature, so perm; problems exporting shared content would be export.

perm.name: Row-level data access rules
perm.summary: Row-level rules that hide all data, too much data or the wrong data because user attributes are missing, team rules combine permissively, static store lists go stale or company-wide tiles are scoped per user.
perm.boundary_note: Charts may look empty or totals may differ, but the cause is access scope rather than rendering or calculation, so perm rather than render or data_quality.

perm.name: Custom role definitions
perm.summary: Custom roles that lack newly introduced permissions, cannot be deleted, bundle legacy permissions, hit the plan's role limit, or do not cover personal spaces or role assignment as expected.
perm.boundary_note: Defining what a role may do is core perm.

perm.name: Folder permission inheritance
perm.summary: Moving content between folders replaces explicit permissions, restricted subfolders do not block inherited editors, overlapping grants confuse admins, or moves are blocked by rights on the destination.
perm.boundary_note: Inheritance of access rights is perm.

perm.name: Permission propagation and caching
perm.summary: Role or membership changes that apply only after minutes, hours or a new session; cached denial pages; nightly-only directory pulls; and access reports built from stale snapshots.
perm.boundary_note: The access rules are right but applied or displayed late; the outcome is still who can access what, so perm.

perm.name: Missing or over-broad permission checks
perm.summary: Actions that bypass or misapply the intended check: duplicating restricted dashboards, shortcuts calling unprotected endpoints, search exposing restricted titles, creators locked out of their own content, or grants surviving group deletion.
perm.boundary_note: These are authorization defects inside the product, so perm rather than auth (identity) or api (public API).

perm.name: Content ownership and transfer
perm.summary: Ownership transfers that leave datasets behind, cannot target the intended user, include private drafts, or leave folders with no owner able to manage sharing.
perm.boundary_note: Ownership determines who can manage and reach content, so perm; scheduled report side effects would be export.

perm.name: Administrative and delegated admin roles
perm.summary: Last-admin protection, recovery when no admin remains, delegated user managers able to grant too much, audit log access held in a separate role, dual approval for privileged changes, and finance users needing a narrow billing role.
perm.boundary_note: These concern who holds administrative rights, so perm; plan or invoice disputes would be billing.

perm.name: Guest and external partner access
perm.summary: Guest access expiring by default, guest domain allow-lists, guests seeing too much of the member directory, drill-through targets not shared with guests, and guests converted to members keeping guest restrictions.
perm.boundary_note: Guest allow-lists are access policies, not network allow-lists, so perm rather than connectivity.

perm.name: Access requests and approvals
perm.summary: Access requests that go unanswered, cannot be made, grant more than was asked for, notify too many people, or are auto-approved by an over-broad rule.
perm.boundary_note: The request and approval workflow decides who gets access, so perm.

perf.name: Missing or regressed database indexes
perf.summary: A migration, table rebuild or new access pattern leaves a hot query without a usable index, so dashboard loads, filters or drill-downs fall back to full scans and become slow as the customer's tables grow.
perf.boundary_note: The data and visuals are correct and nothing fails outright; the only problem is latency caused by query execution, so it is perf rather than render or data_quality.

perf.name: Query result cache misses and invalidation storms
perf.summary: Cache keys that are too granular, invalidation that fires on every small write, or a cache that is cold after a deploy cause every viewer to hit the database, giving slow and inconsistent load times.
perf.boundary_note: When a cache returns wrong or stale content it is render; here the cache returns correct data but too rarely, so the symptom is purely speed.

perf.name: Report and export job queue backlog
perf.summary: Shared worker pools for scheduled reports and large exports get blocked by oversized jobs, peak-hour bursts or retries, so deliveries arrive hours late even though each file is eventually correct.
perf.boundary_note: Wrong export contents or failed delivery addresses are export; lateness caused by queue capacity and contention is perf.

perf.name: Browser-side slowness with very large result sets
perf.summary: Tables, pivots and charts that send tens of thousands of rows or points to the browser freeze the tab, scroll slowly or trigger 'page unresponsive' warnings, while the server query itself is quick.
perf.boundary_note: The visual is eventually drawn correctly; the issue is client CPU and memory cost, so it is perf rather than render.

perf.name: High-cardinality grouping and unbounded queries
perf.summary: Grouping by dimensions with hundreds of thousands of values, or queries with no date bound, produce enormous intermediate results that time out or exhaust query memory.
perf.boundary_note: Timeouts here come from query load and data volume rather than wrong calculations (data_quality) or API contract errors (api).

perf.name: Tenant query concurrency limits and shared compute contention
perf.summary: Per-workspace concurrency slots or shared compute pools are saturated by scheduled jobs, bulk refreshes or a neighbouring heavy workload, so interactive queries wait in a queue with 'waiting for capacity' messages.
perf.boundary_note: Requests are queued for capacity rather than rejected for quota (api rate limits) or permission (perm).

perf.name: Rollup and precomputation refresh overruns
perf.summary: Nightly rollup tables or pre-aggregated cubes take longer than their window after data growth or a backfill, so business-hours queries fall back to raw tables or wait on refresh locks.
perf.boundary_note: The ingestion itself completed (not sync) and the rolled-up values are correct (not data_quality); the problem is how long the precomputation runs and what it slows down.

perf.name: Expensive calculated fields and custom formulas
perf.summary: Customer-defined calculated metrics using nested lookups, regex matching, per-row date parsing or running totals over unbounded windows are evaluated row by row at query time and slow dashboards drastically.
perf.boundary_note: The formula results are correct; when a formula returns wrong numbers it is data_quality, but when it only costs time it is perf.

perf.name: Dashboard auto-refresh and widget fan-out overload
perf.summary: Very short auto-refresh intervals, dozens of widgets per dashboard and many open screens multiply query volume until the workspace's own refreshes slow everything down.
perf.boundary_note: This is load generated by the product's own dashboard behaviour, not a display defect (render) or an API client exceeding limits (api).

perf.name: Slow filter value lists, search and autocomplete
perf.summary: Filter dropdowns, global search and autocomplete fields scan full dimension tables or unindexed text on every keystroke, so pickers take many seconds to populate.
perf.boundary_note: Filters that apply the wrong values are render; pickers that are merely slow to populate are perf.

perf.name: Stale table statistics and bad query plans
perf.summary: After a large backfill, purge or bulk import, table statistics no longer reflect reality and the query planner picks nested loops or wrong join orders, making previously fast queries slow overnight.
perf.boundary_note: Indexes exist and data is correct; the plan choice under changed data volume is a performance problem rather than a sync or data_quality one.

perf.name: Memory growth in long-running browser sessions
perf.summary: Dashboards left open for hours on wall displays or kiosk screens accumulate chart instances, listeners or cached responses with every refresh until the browser becomes sluggish or crashes.
perf.boundary_note: The dashboard renders correctly at first and degrades only over time because of resource growth, which is perf rather than render.

perf.name: Oversized page payloads and uncached static assets
perf.summary: Dashboard definitions bloated with embedded images or history, or front-end assets served without long-lived cache headers, make every page open download megabytes before anything appears.
perf.boundary_note: Pages load slowly but successfully over a working network; blocked or unreachable hosts would be connectivity.

api.name: Webhook delivery timeouts and retry exhaustion
api.summary: Customer endpoints that respond slowly, redirect, reject large bodies or are offline longer than the retry schedule cause webhook deliveries to be marked failed, retried or eventually dropped.
api.boundary_note: These are generic product webhooks consumed by customer systems; webhooks used as an alert notification channel belong to alerts.

api.name: Webhook signature verification failures
api.summary: Receivers reject genuine webhooks because the raw body is altered before HMAC verification, the signing secret was rotated unevenly, the receiver's clock drifts, or the verification code signs the wrong content.
api.boundary_note: This is message-integrity verification on integration traffic, not user sign-in (auth) or TLS certificate trust (connectivity).

api.name: Rate limiting and 429 handling
api.summary: Integrations receive HTTP 429 because limits are shared across an organisation, burst limits are exceeded by parallel calls, heavy endpoints have lower limits, or clients ignore Retry-After.
api.boundary_note: Requests are rejected by documented quotas rather than slowed by platform load (perf).

api.name: Pagination consistency
api.summary: Clients paging through collections miss or repeat records because of offset paging over changing data, expired cursors, silently capped page sizes or non-unique sort keys.
api.boundary_note: The stored data is correct; records are lost or duplicated only in how the client walks the API, so this is api rather than data_quality or export.

api.name: Integration API key ownership, scope and expiry
api.summary: Keys used by scripts and integrations stop working because they were tied to a deactivated person, lack a needed scope, expired under a rotation policy, or belong to a different environment.
api.boundary_note: Keys here authenticate machine integrations against the public API; a person's own sign-in, SSO or personal API-key login problems belong to auth.

api.name: Request validation and payload format errors
api.summary: Requests are rejected with 400, 413, 415 or 422 because of non-ISO dates, missing content types, enum casing, unknown fields, oversized batches or unencoded query values.
api.boundary_note: The API is rejecting or misreading the caller's request format; failures of connected-source ingestion jobs are sync.

api.name: API versioning, deprecations and sunsets
api.summary: Integrations break or change behaviour when a version reaches sunset, fields are renamed between versions, or the default version for unpinned requests differs from what the client expects.
api.boundary_note: These are contract changes in the public API, not export file format changes (export) or product UI changes.

api.name: Server-side 5xx defects for specific request shapes
api.summary: Particular inputs such as unusual characters, empty resources, oversized URLs, stale references or deploy-time connection draining make otherwise working endpoints return 500, 502 or 503.
api.boundary_note: The error is raised by the API service itself for a specific request, not by sustained load (perf) or blocked network paths (connectivity).

api.name: Idempotency, retries and concurrent write safety
api.summary: Client retries without idempotency keys create duplicate objects, keys are reused with different bodies or after expiry, and concurrent updates overwrite each other without conditional requests.
api.boundary_note: Duplicates come from how API writes are retried, not from inbound connector re-syncs (sync).

api.name: Webhook event ordering, duplication and coalescing
api.summary: At-least-once delivery, unordered delivery, batched payloads and event coalescing surprise consumers that assume exactly-once, in-order, one-event-per-change delivery.
api.boundary_note: These are semantics of the general event stream for integrations; alert notification duplicates belong to alerts.

api.name: Webhook subscription configuration and auto-disable
api.summary: Events never arrive or arrive twice because subscriptions were auto-disabled after failures, cover the wrong event types, filter out new objects, or are registered twice.
api.boundary_note: Configuration of the integration event subscription, not the alert channel configuration (alerts) or export schedules (export).

api.name: Numeric, timestamp and null serialization in responses
api.summary: Correct stored values are misread by clients because of 64-bit integer precision loss, UTC timestamps, decimals returned as strings, fractional percentages or omitted null fields.
api.boundary_note: Values are correct in the product and in the response; the problem is serialization and client parsing, so it is api rather than data_quality.

api.name: Asynchronous bulk job endpoints
api.summary: Bulk import, export and async query jobs confuse clients through expiring result URLs, partial-success states, multi-part results, stuck statuses and removed callback parameters.
api.boundary_note: These are API job mechanics used by customer code; scheduled report deliveries and UI exports are export.

alerts.name: Threshold and comparison misconfiguration
alerts.summary: Rules compare against the wrong unit, currency, operator, boundary or baseline period, or lose their threshold through an editor defect, so alerts fire constantly or never.
alerts.boundary_note: The metric values are correct and only the rule definition is wrong, so this is alerts rather than data_quality.

alerts.name: Evaluation window and aggregation mismatch
alerts.summary: Rolling versus calendar windows, sum versus average, tiny samples, week definitions and 'for' durations make a rule evaluate something different from what the customer reads on the dashboard.
alerts.boundary_note: The dashboard numbers are right; the alert evaluates a different window or aggregate, which is a rule configuration matter for alerts rather than data_quality or render.

alerts.name: Evaluation timing versus data arrival
alerts.summary: Rules evaluate before the latest batch of data has landed or re-evaluate old periods when delayed data catches up, causing false drops, missed spikes or bursts of stale alerts.
alerts.boundary_note: Data arrives on its normal schedule (not sync); the problem is when the alert evaluates relative to that arrival.

alerts.name: Suppression, mute and maintenance windows
alerts.summary: Maintenance windows in the wrong time zone, snoozes applied too broadly, mutes that never expire and missing dependency suppression lead to alerts during planned work or silence during real incidents.
alerts.boundary_note: Concerns when alert notifications are deliberately held back, a capability that exists only in the alerting feature.

alerts.name: Duplicate alert notifications
alerts.summary: Cloned rules, overlapping recipient lists, short re-notify intervals and double evaluation during scheduler failover send the same alert more than once.
alerts.boundary_note: Duplicated alert notifications are alerts; duplicated generic webhook events for integrations are api and duplicated synced records are sync.

alerts.name: Flapping alerts and missing hysteresis
alerts.summary: Metrics hovering around a threshold, noisy minute-level data, gaps treated as recovery and severity thresholds set too close together cause repeated fire and resolve cycles.
alerts.boundary_note: The metric itself is behaving normally; the rule lacks recovery thresholds, smoothing or pending periods, which is alerts configuration.

alerts.name: Email channel delivery of alerts
alerts.summary: Alert emails are delayed, quarantined, bounced, suppressed, mis-templated or missing images because of sender authentication, list policies, suppression lists, digest settings or template variables.
alerts.boundary_note: Covers emails that carry alert notifications only; password-reset emails are auth and scheduled report emails are export.

alerts.name: Chat-tool channel delivery of alerts
alerts.summary: Alert posts to the customer's chat tool fail because the app's token was revoked, the app is not in a private channel, the channel was archived or messages exceed size limits.
alerts.boundary_note: Delivery of alert notifications into a chat tool is alerts; it is not an inbound data sync or a generic API problem.

alerts.name: Webhook channel delivery of alerts
alerts.summary: Alert webhooks to on-call or automation tools fail or misbehave because of payload templates producing invalid JSON, rotated routing keys, unstable dedup keys, slow receivers or payload format changes.
alerts.boundary_note: These webhooks carry alert notifications through an alert channel; general product event webhooks and their subscriptions are api.

alerts.name: No-data and missing-data handling
alerts.summary: Rules treat missing data as OK, as zero, or as an alert condition in ways that hide feed outages, fire for closed stores or sparse metrics, or leave rules stuck on a retired dataset.
alerts.boundary_note: Restoring a failed feed is sync; deciding how an alert rule behaves when data is absent is alerts.

alerts.name: Anomaly detection baselines and sensitivity
alerts.summary: Dynamic-baseline alerts are distorted by holiday peaks, promotions, short history, model resets or overly high sensitivity, producing noise or silence.
alerts.boundary_note: The detected values are correct; the issue is how the anomaly alert's baseline is learned and tuned.

alerts.name: Rule scope, segment filters and per-group evaluation
alerts.summary: Rules are scoped with renamed filter values, frozen segments, missing per-store grouping, closed stores or filters not inherited from dashboards, so they watch the wrong population.
alerts.boundary_note: This is the alert rule's own scope; filters that fail to apply on a dashboard are render and access restrictions are perm.

alerts.name: Recipient routing and escalation
alerts.summary: Alerts reach the wrong people or no one because of static recipients after staff changes, mis-ordered severity routes, wrong routing placeholders, recipient limits, stale push tokens or acknowledgements triggered by link scanners.
alerts.boundary_note: Deciding who receives an alert notification is alerts; who may view data or dashboards is perm.

alerts.name: Alert schedules, active hours and time zones
alerts.summary: Active hours, digests and holiday handling in alert rules use the wrong time zone, ignore daylight saving changes or cannot follow each store's local time.
alerts.boundary_note: These are time settings inside alert rules and channels; the workspace's own default time zone and locale settings are workspace_admin.

data_quality.name: Currency conversion errors
data_quality.summary: Amounts are converted to the reporting currency with the wrong rate date, an inverted rate, a second conversion of already-converted amounts, or a defaulted source currency. Symptoms are closed periods that drift between runs or revenue off by an FX-sized factor.
data_quality.boundary_note: Orders were ingested completely and on time; the error is in the conversion maths applied afterwards, so it is not sync. Choosing which reporting currency to show is workspace_admin.

data_quality.name: Time-zone bucketing of transactions
data_quality.summary: Transactions land in the wrong day or hour because aggregates use UTC boundaries, a wrongly mapped store zone, naive timestamps read as UTC or DST-unaware hour labels. Symptoms are evening sales on the next day, shifted hourly peaks and month-end mismatches.
data_quality.boundary_note: All rows are present (a sync window gap that loses rows is sync) and the chart faithfully draws the stored aggregates (not render). A workspace time-zone preference left at the wrong value is workspace_admin.

data_quality.name: Source field mapping to metrics
data_quality.summary: A correctly ingested source field feeds the wrong metric: gross order total as net revenue, line count as units, discount as tax, session id as customer id, or VAT-inclusive prices read as net. Symptoms are systematically inflated or deflated KPIs.
data_quality.boundary_note: The connector delivered every field; the defect is which field feeds which metric, not a failed or partial sync.

data_quality.name: Dimension and category mapping
data_quality.summary: Lookup tables and rule-based mappings for categories, regions, channels and product hierarchies misassign records through missing prefixes, name collisions, rule ordering or non-effective-dated changes. Symptoms are growing 'Uncategorized' buckets, rewritten regional history or merged categories.
data_quality.boundary_note: Records are classified incorrectly after ingestion; who can see a dimension is perm, and how a correct grouping is drawn on screen is render.

data_quality.name: Deduplication and identity resolution logic
data_quality.summary: Matching rules used to count distinct customers or transactions are too aggressive (placeholder emails, same amount and timestamp) or too lax (case-sensitive email, shipments counted as orders). Symptoms are under- or over-counted customers and orders.
data_quality.boundary_note: Each record was ingested exactly once; rows inserted twice by a re-sync are sync, whereas this family covers the matching and counting logic applied afterwards.

data_quality.name: Ratio and distinct-count aggregation
data_quality.summary: Rollups average pre-computed ratios, add up non-additive distinct counts, approximate medians or use an incomplete denominator. Symptoms are KPIs that change with drill level or exceed plausible ranges.
data_quality.boundary_note: Inputs are correct and the chart plots what it receives; the defect is in aggregation maths, so it is neither render nor perf.

data_quality.name: Rounding and numeric precision
data_quality.summary: Line-level rounding, truncation, binary floating-point sums, a different rounding mode and truncated FX rate precision create cent-level or proportional differences against finance systems.
data_quality.boundary_note: The computed values themselves are off and reconcile wrongly through every surface; rounding only a displayed label is render, and number display preferences are workspace_admin.

data_quality.name: Units and scale interpretation
data_quality.summary: Values are read in the wrong unit: minor versus major currency units, zero-decimal currencies, cases versus single units, grams versus kilograms. Symptoms are figures off by exact factors such as 100, 12 or 1000, or impossible negatives.
data_quality.boundary_note: Values arrived intact and nothing failed to load; their unit interpretation is wrong, so this is not sync.

data_quality.name: Refunds, returns and revenue netting
data_quality.summary: Net revenue logic double-subtracts partial refunds, attributes returns to an unexpected date, treats exchanges as refunds, ignores some refund methods or counts gift card value twice.
data_quality.boundary_note: These are metric-definition and netting errors on correctly ingested transactions; an export using a different filter default than the dashboard is export.

data_quality.name: Calculated fields and null handling
data_quality.summary: Custom metric formulas evaluate incorrectly: nulls coerced to zero, divide-by-zero returning 0, integer division, parentheses lost in a formula migration, or stale references after a metric rename.
data_quality.boundary_note: The formula engine produces wrong numbers from correct inputs; permission to edit calculated fields is perm.

data_quality.name: Period comparison alignment
data_quality.summary: Year-over-year, like-for-like and to-date comparisons pair the wrong periods: calendar date instead of fiscal weekday, leap-day shifts, partial versus full periods, or wrong comparable-store eligibility.
data_quality.boundary_note: Calendar settings were configured correctly and the comparison engine applied them wrongly; a fiscal calendar left unset is workspace_admin.

data_quality.name: Semi-additive measures
data_quality.summary: Snapshot measures such as stock on hand, active members and balances are summed across time, taken at the wrong point in the period or rolled up at the wrong grain. Symptoms are values that scale with the length of the date range.
data_quality.boundary_note: Snapshots were ingested correctly; the time-aggregation rule is wrong, so this is not sync or render.

data_quality.name: Join fan-out and double counting
data_quality.summary: One-to-many joins (orders to promotion codes, customers to addresses, order-level fees to line items, monthly targets to daily rows) multiply measures.
data_quality.boundary_note: Storage holds no duplicate rows, so it is not sync; the duplication happens in the query model that joins tables.

data_quality.name: Text normalisation and key matching
data_quality.summary: Keys and labels are altered or compared inconsistently: trailing spaces, letter case, Unicode forms, leading zeros stripped by type inference, identifiers mangled into scientific notation. Symptoms are split groups and 'Unknown product' rows.
data_quality.boundary_note: Files and records loaded successfully; values were normalised or typed incorrectly, which breaks joins and grouping after ingestion.

connectivity.name: Product egress addresses blocked by customer firewalls
connectivity.summary: Connectors pulling from customer-hosted sources fail when the customer's firewall, API gateway or intrusion prevention system does not allow the product's published egress ranges (a newly added range, a too-narrow entry, geo-blocking, automatic IPS blocks). Symptoms are timeouts, resets or 403s on some or all runs.
connectivity.boundary_note: Data is not arriving because packets are dropped or refused by network policy; credentials and source data are fine, so this is not sync or auth.

connectivity.name: Corporate proxy behaviour
connectivity.summary: The customer's explicit proxy blocks WebSocket upgrades, is bypassed by non-browser tools, enforces short response timeouts or requires its own authentication. Symptoms are frozen live tiles, tool timeouts, 504 pages from the proxy and 407 responses.
connectivity.boundary_note: The product works from other networks and fails only through the proxy path; product-side slowness is perf and product sign-in failures are auth.

connectivity.name: TLS inspection appliances
connectivity.summary: Inspection devices re-sign traffic with corporate CAs that client tools do not trust, use weak or expired inspection CAs, or reset large inspected uploads. Symptoms are certificate errors limited to the corporate network.
connectivity.boundary_note: Certificate trust breaks on the network path and is fixed with correct trust chains and appliance configuration, never by disabling verification; credentials are not involved.

connectivity.name: DNS resolution
connectivity.summary: Stale resolver caches, overridden TTLs, split-horizon zones, filtering resolvers, hosts-file entries, VPN resolvers and product-side DNSSEC mistakes stop names resolving to the right addresses.
connectivity.boundary_note: Name resolution is a reachability problem; whether product links display a custom domain is a workspace_admin setting.

connectivity.name: Certificates on customer source endpoints
connectivity.summary: Customer-hosted APIs, FTPS and file endpoints that connectors read from present incomplete chains, expired certificates, hostname mismatches or privately issued certificates, so the connector cannot establish a trusted TLS session.
connectivity.boundary_note: The TLS handshake to the source fails; an expired OAuth token or a connector logic error would be sync.

connectivity.name: Webhook delivery reachability
connectivity.summary: Outbound webhook calls to customer receivers are dropped or rejected by firewalls, web application firewalls, internal-only DNS names, unsupported TLS versions, incomplete certificate chains or disallowed ports.
connectivity.boundary_note: Payloads, schemas and retry logic are correct; delivery fails at the network or TLS layer. Payload, rate-limit or retry defects are api.

connectivity.name: Embedded dashboard blocking
connectivity.summary: Embedded dashboards never display because the host page's Content-Security-Policy, the workspace's allowed embed origins, mixed content or a kiosk webview's domain allow-list block the frame.
connectivity.boundary_note: The frame is blocked by browser or network policy before anything is drawn; an embed that loads but draws visuals wrongly is render, and who may view it is perm.

connectivity.name: TLS protocol and cipher compatibility
connectivity.summary: Legacy clients or source servers limited to TLS 1.0/1.1, hardened cipher policies without a shared suite, or clients that omit SNI fail handshakes with the product or its connectors.
connectivity.boundary_note: Handshake failures are transport compatibility problems, not authentication or API errors.

connectivity.name: Identity provider endpoint reachability
connectivity.summary: The product cannot fetch IdP metadata, discovery or signing-key endpoints, or users' browsers cannot reach an on-premises IdP, so sign-in or certificate rollovers fail.
connectivity.boundary_note: Assertions and attribute mappings are correct; the failing step is reaching the IdP endpoint over the network, so this is connectivity rather than auth.

connectivity.name: Custom domain DNS and certificates
connectivity.summary: Custom domains break when certificate validation records are deleted, CAA records block issuance, records point to retired targets or IP addresses, or changes are made in a non-authoritative zone.
connectivity.boundary_note: The domain does not resolve or serve a valid certificate; whether links and emails use the custom domain is a workspace_admin setting.

connectivity.name: Data agent egress to ingestion endpoints
connectivity.summary: On-premises data agents and upload tools are blocked by egress rules missing regional or control-plane hostnames, legacy ports, IP-based rules that miss anycast addresses, or NAT port exhaustion.
connectivity.boundary_note: The agent cannot reach the product's ingestion endpoints at all; once connected, slow, partial or duplicated ingestion is sync.

connectivity.name: Workspace IP allow-list
connectivity.summary: The workspace-level IP allow-list blocks legitimate users after public IP changes, CIDR mistakes, split-tunnel VPN routing or an IPv6 rollout.
connectivity.boundary_note: Users authenticate correctly and are refused by network-location policy; role-based access to content is perm.

connectivity.name: IPv6, MTU and routing paths
connectivity.summary: Broken IPv6 routes, path-MTU black holes on tunnels, IPv6-only segments without DNS64/NAT64 and asymmetric routing cause hangs and resets on particular networks only.
connectivity.boundary_note: Failures follow the network path, not product load (perf) or session lifetime (auth).

connectivity.name: Web filtering and secure web gateways
connectivity.summary: Secure web gateways, data-loss prevention rules, managed browser extensions and mis-assigned filtering policies block product hostnames, uploads or downloads.
connectivity.boundary_note: Access is denied by the customer's content filtering, not by product permissions, authentication or export logic.

workspace_admin.name: Workspace name and identity
workspace_admin.summary: Workspace display name, URL name, legal name and distinguishing labels are stale, truncated, wrongly encoded or ambiguous. Symptoms are old names in tabs, footers and emails, broken bookmarks after a URL rename and confusion between similarly named workspaces.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Concerns how the organisation identifies itself in the product, not who may access it (perm) or what it pays (billing).

workspace_admin.name: Logo and branding
workspace_admin.summary: Logo uploads, logo variants and brand themes do not appear as intended because the SVG sanitiser removes linked resources, files are low resolution, a dark-mode variant is missing or branding toggles for public links are set the wrong way.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Organisational branding settings; charts drawing data incorrectly are render and who can open a shared link is perm.

workspace_admin.name: Custom domain display settings
workspace_admin.summary: A verified custom domain is not used in generated links and emails, the default domain keeps serving the workspace, or a rollout mode limits branded links, because link-domain, redirect or rollout settings are off.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: DNS and certificates are healthy; when the domain itself fails to resolve or serves a bad certificate, that is connectivity.

workspace_admin.name: Language and locale
workspace_admin.summary: Interface language, locale variant, language source and enforcement, translations of custom labels, email language and sorting collation follow the wrong setting.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Preference settings of the organisation; wrong values or calculations behind the labels would be data_quality.

workspace_admin.name: Number formats
workspace_admin.summary: Decimal and thousands separators, digit grouping, negative-number style, default precision and compact abbreviations differ from what the organisation expects.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Values are correct and only formatted according to settings; rounding inside calculations is data_quality and broken chart drawing is render.

workspace_admin.name: Date formats and week conventions
workspace_admin.summary: Day/month order, relative versus absolute timestamps, 12/24-hour clock, week start day and period label style follow the wrong workspace default.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Display and calendar conventions chosen by the organisation; mis-bucketing by the engine is data_quality and failed report delivery is export.

workspace_admin.name: Time-zone preferences
workspace_admin.summary: Workspace, dashboard or personal time-zone preferences left at the UTC default, set to fixed offsets or following the device shift relative-date filters, schedules and day boundaries.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: The engine applies the configured zone correctly; if it ignored a correct setting the issue would be data_quality.

workspace_admin.name: Fiscal year settings
workspace_admin.summary: Fiscal start month, fiscal year label convention, retail 4-5-4 calendar and 53rd-week placement are not configured to match the organisation's financial calendar.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Organisational calendar configuration; comparisons that ignore a correctly configured calendar are data_quality.

workspace_admin.name: Default dashboards and landing pages
workspace_admin.summary: Workspace, team, new-member and mobile home dashboards and the default date range point to archived content or are overridden by other landing settings.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Organisational defaults, not access rights; users who cannot see a dashboard because of their role belong to perm.

workspace_admin.name: Reporting currency settings
workspace_admin.summary: Reporting currency, secondary display currency, currency display style and per-report currency overrides are set incorrectly, missing, or still recomputing after a change.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Conversion maths is correct; wrong rates or double conversion are data_quality, and the currency of the customer's own subscription charges is billing.

workspace_admin.name: System email identity
workspace_admin.summary: Sender display name, reply-to address, sender domain verification, footer address and email header logo for system emails are not configured.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: The identity of organisational emails; scheduled report delivery is export and password-reset emails are auth.

workspace_admin.name: Settings inheritance and overrides
workspace_admin.summary: Personal preferences, workspace templates and locked parent-organisation settings take precedence over or replace workspace defaults, so changes appear not to apply.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Precedence among organisational and personal settings, not permission to change them (perm).

workspace_admin.name: Settings audit and accidental changes
workspace_admin.summary: Workspace settings changed by mistake, by imports, by copy operations or by the customer's own automation, and how admins trace, restore and get notified about such changes.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Administration of organisational settings; metric threshold notifications are alerts and role changes are perm.

workspace_admin.name: Business calendar and trading hours
workspace_admin.summary: Holiday calendars, weekend definitions, regional calendars, calendar year coverage and store trading hours used by working-day and per-hour metrics are missing or wrong.
workspace_admin.boundary_note: Organisational calendar settings; when correct calendar settings are mis-applied by calculations, that is data_quality.

auth-g01.shared_root_cause: The customer's inbound email security scanner follows links in incoming mail and redeems the single-use password reset token before the user clicks it.

auth-g02.shared_root_cause: The customer's identity provider rotated its SAML signing certificate while the workspace SSO settings still trusted the old certificate.

auth-g03.shared_root_cause: The user's device clock drifted outside the TOTP validity window, so generated codes were rejected.

auth-g04.shared_root_cause: An unattended process (scheduled script, old add-in or kiosk browser autofill) keeps retrying an outdated password and trips the lockout policy.

auth-g05.shared_root_cause: Browsers block cookies set inside a cross-site iframe, so dashboards embedded in a customer portal cannot keep a session and loop back to the sign-in form.

auth-g06.shared_root_cause: The user's primary email changed in the identity provider, so SSO matching by email no longer finds the existing account.

auth-g07.shared_root_cause: Resetting or changing a password revokes all of the user's personal access tokens by design, breaking tools that still hold the old token.

auth-g08.shared_root_cause: The OIDC client secret in the customer's identity provider app registration expired, so the token exchange is rejected.

auth-g09.shared_root_cause: One session cookie was shared across workspaces, so signing in to a second workspace replaced the first workspace's session.

sync-g01.shared_root_cause: The user who authorized the connector was deactivated or removed in the source system, which revoked the OAuth grant the connector depended on.

sync-g02.shared_root_cause: The source system assigns new record IDs when records are merged or re-imported, so upserting by external ID inserts them as new rows.

sync-g03.shared_root_cause: The source changes records through bulk or import tools without updating their last-modified timestamp, so the incremental sync skips them.

sync-g04.shared_root_cause: A custom field was renamed or recreated in the source, leaving the connector's field mapping pointing at a name that no longer exists.

sync-g05.shared_root_cause: Files saved on computers with European regional settings use semicolon separators and decimal commas, which the importer parsed with default assumptions.

sync-g06.shared_root_cause: Other applications consume the customer CRM's shared daily API allowance, so the connector runs out of quota partway through a run.

sync-g07.shared_root_cause: The connection auto-paused after consecutive failures and its failure notifications went to an inactive user, so nobody noticed.

sync-g08.shared_root_cause: The event signing secret was rotated in the commerce platform but not in the connector, so every inbound event was rejected and only the scheduled sync delivered data.

sync-g09.shared_root_cause: A cancelled run left its job lock in place, so later runs waited on it or refused to start.

render-g01.shared_root_cause: The chart component treated a series whose values were all null as invalid and drew nothing instead of an empty state.

render-g02.shared_root_cause: The service worker kept serving the application bundle cached before a release until every tab of the app was closed.

render-g03.shared_root_cause: Widgets had a date range pinned in their own settings, overriding the dashboard date filter, and the override indicator was easy to miss or hidden.

render-g04.shared_root_cause: Series colours were assigned by position in the result rather than by category value, so colours shifted when categories were missing or reordered.

render-g05.shared_root_cause: Large charts on high-resolution Apple displays exceeded Safari's canvas size or memory limit and silently failed to draw.

render-g06.shared_root_cause: Time-axis labels were formatted in the viewer's browser time zone while the data was bucketed in the workspace time zone.

render-g07.shared_root_cause: Tabs opened before a release requested code chunks that the release had removed, so the affected widgets failed to load.

render-g08.shared_root_cause: The virtualized table computed row geometry assuming 100% browser zoom, so rows and headers drifted apart at other zoom levels.

billing-g01.shared_root_cause: After a seat-counting rule change, users in 'invited' status were counted as billable seats, so unaccepted invitations inflated seat totals.

billing-g02.shared_root_cause: Mid-cycle seat additions, upgrades and add-ons were prorated from the start of the billing period instead of the date of the change.

billing-g03.shared_root_cause: Discounts were attached to a single subscription term rather than to the customer account, so renewal terms were generated without them.

billing-g04.shared_root_cause: The card issuer's 3-D Secure challenge opened in a popup that the browser blocked, so the new card was never verified or attached.

billing-g05.shared_root_cause: A small verification authorization placed when a card is saved looked to customers like an extra charge, although it is never captured.

billing-g06.shared_root_cause: VAT IDs entered without the country prefix or with spaces or dots failed validation, so VAT was charged instead of reverse charge.

billing-g07.shared_root_cause: The data-rows usage meter kept counting rows from disconnected, archived or soft-deleted sources during their retention window.

billing-g08.shared_root_cause: Contracted prices were stored as overrides covering only the first term, so renewal invoices and quotes reverted to list price.

billing-g09.shared_root_cause: The billing contact used for dunning emails still pointed to a departed employee's mailbox, so payment failure reminders were never seen.

export-g01.shared_root_cause: Older schedules stored a fixed UTC offset instead of the named time zone, so delivery times shifted by an hour when daylight saving began or ended.

export-g02.shared_root_cause: Recipients' mail security systems pre-fetched links in report emails, consuming single-use download tokens before the person clicked.

export-g03.shared_root_cause: CSV exports were written as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark, so desktop spreadsheet software decoded non-ASCII characters with a legacy code page.

export-g04.shared_root_cause: Exports were generated from the dashboard's saved filter state, ignoring filters the user applied in the current session without saving.

export-g05.shared_root_cause: The headless PDF renderer captured the dashboard before lazy-loaded or slow widgets had finished loading.

export-g06.shared_root_cause: The file-drop filename template had no date or timestamp token, so each run overwrote the previous file.

export-g07.shared_root_cause: Excel exports were truncated at the worksheet row limit of 1,048,576 rows without splitting the data or warning the user.

export-g08.shared_root_cause: The workspace data protection policy masks or removes fields tagged as personal data in every export, including scheduled ones.

perm-g01.shared_root_cause: The group-to-role mapping compared directory group names case-sensitively, so a change in capitalisation stopped the mapping from matching and users fell back to the default role.

perm-g02.shared_root_cause: The row-level rule filters by the user's store_id attribute, which SSO just-in-time provisioning did not populate, so affected users saw no rows.

perm-g03.shared_root_cause: Permissions were evaluated once per session and cached, so role and membership changes applied only after a new session or cache expiry.

perm-g04.shared_root_cause: Moving content into a folder replaced its explicit dashboard-level permissions with the destination folder's inherited permissions.

perm-g05.shared_root_cause: Public share links were not tied to their creator's status, so links created by deactivated or deprovisioned users stayed active.

perm-g06.shared_root_cause: Guest invitations defaulted to a 30-day expiry that inviters did not change, so guest access ended unexpectedly.

perm-g07.shared_root_cause: Access requests were routed only to the dashboard owner, whose account had been deactivated, so requests went unseen.

perm-g08.shared_root_cause: The ownership transfer tool moved dashboards but not the private datasets they were built on, which stayed with the deactivated previous owner.

perf-g01.shared_root_cause: After the orders table moved to automatic monthly partitions, newly created partitions were missing the (store_id, order_date) index, so any query touching recent months scanned those partitions fully while older months stayed fast.

perf-g02.shared_root_cause: The widget result cache key included the viewer's session identifier, so identical queries from different users and new sessions never reused a cached result.

perf-g03.shared_root_cause: The shared report worker pool processed jobs strictly first-in-first-out, so a single multi-hour full-history export blocked every smaller scheduled report queued behind it.

perf-g04.shared_root_cause: Scheduled report renders and interactive dashboard queries drew from the same per-workspace concurrency slots, so a burst of reports scheduled at the top of the hour starved interactive users.

perf-g05.shared_root_cause: A multi-year historical backfill made the nightly rollup refresh rebuild every partition instead of only changed ones, pushing the refresh into business hours.

perf-g06.shared_root_cause: Table statistics were not refreshed after a bulk import of several years of history, so the planner kept estimating tiny row counts and chose nested-loop joins.

perf-g07.shared_root_cause: The chart component created a new tooltip and resize listener on every auto-refresh without disposing of the previous ones, so memory grew steadily on screens left open.

perf-g08.shared_root_cause: Dashboards configured with a 30-second auto-refresh kept re-running every widget query even when the browser tab was hidden, multiplying load across many open screens.

api-g01.shared_root_cause: A JSON body-parsing middleware in the customer's receiving service parsed and re-serialized the webhook body before signature verification, so the HMAC was computed over different bytes than were signed.

api-g02.shared_root_cause: The organisation-wide request quota is shared by all API keys in the workspace, and a status-polling script calling the API every second consumed most of it, starving other integrations.

api-g03.shared_root_cause: The client paged through a frequently changing collection with offset pagination, so inserts and updates during the walk shifted rows between pages, skipping some and repeating others.

api-g04.shared_root_cause: Integration keys had been created under a person's account, and deactivating that person during offboarding correctly revoked every key they owned.

api-g05.shared_root_cause: The v1 reports endpoints reached their announced sunset date and now return 410 Gone, but the integration had not been migrated to v2.

api-g06.shared_root_cause: The webhook subscription was automatically disabled after 72 hours of consecutive delivery failures, and it stayed disabled after the customer's endpoint recovered because nobody re-enabled it.

api-g07.shared_root_cause: Order and line identifiers are 64-bit integers returned as JSON numbers, and the customer's JavaScript code parsed them as double-precision numbers, rounding IDs above 2^53.

api-g08.shared_root_cause: The customer's HTTP client retried POST requests that had timed out on the client side without sending an Idempotency-Key, so requests that had actually succeeded were executed again.

api-g09.shared_root_cause: Bulk job result download URLs are pre-signed and expire 15 minutes after the job status call that returned them, and the client stored the URL and downloaded it later.

alerts-g01.shared_root_cause: Hourly rules evaluated at minute :00, but the customer's point-of-sale batch for the previous hour lands between :05 and :10, so the latest hour was evaluated while still partial.

alerts-g02.shared_root_cause: Maintenance and mute windows created from the schedule editor were saved in UTC instead of the rule's configured time zone, shifting them by the store's UTC offset.

alerts-g03.shared_root_cause: Cloning a dashboard also cloned the alert rules attached to its widgets, so each rule existed twice with the same recipients.

alerts-g04.shared_root_cause: The chat app's access token was revoked on the customer's chat workspace side (app reinstalled or removed during cleanup), so alert posts were rejected until the channel was reconnected.

alerts-g05.shared_root_cause: The custom alert webhook payload template inserted text fields without JSON escaping, so quotes or line breaks in names and descriptions produced invalid JSON.

alerts-g06.shared_root_cause: The rules used the default no-data behaviour of treating an empty evaluation window as OK, so a source that stopped reporting entirely never triggered the threshold.

alerts-g07.shared_root_cause: The anomaly baseline's training window covered the holiday peak, inflating both the expected level and its variance for the following weeks.

alerts-g08.shared_root_cause: Rules had a single threshold with no recovery threshold or pending period, so a metric hovering around the boundary opened and resolved the alert repeatedly.

alerts-g09.shared_root_cause: Rule active hours were stored as fixed UTC offsets captured at creation, so they shifted by an hour when daylight saving time began or ended.
